findings.name: integrity.event_log_suffix_rewrite_needs_anchor
findings.summary: store-level adversary only (no in-world route): a rewritten suffix and a truncated tail both pass chain verification; they are detectable only by comparing the head hash with a copy kept outside the store, which nothing does today
findings.fix: Keep the head (seq, hash) of every world outside the event table and check it on load: e.g. write it into each experiment's results file and into the snapshot row, and have World.load / `crucible world replay --verify` compare (the store already records a hash per snapshot; `World.load` does not compare the replayed tail's starting point with it). Sign or HMAC snapshot blobs, or replace pickle with the canonical JSON state dump, before stores are shared between machines.

probes.attack: A three-party contract is built so that its activation fails half-way: when the last party signs, the membership clause and a grant clause are applied and then a share-transfer clause fails (more shares than exist). A second case fails inside a nested bank move after an escrow transfer (a bounty funded from an account that is emptied by an earlier clause in the same command is not possible, so the case uses a marketplace order for more than the buyer has after listing fees). Checked: every table is byte-identical before and after the failed command, apart from the rejection record.
probes.summary: both failing commands left every table byte-identical (membership, grant, signature and escrow move were rolled back with the failed nested step)

probes.name: integrity.contract_settlement_consistency
probes.attack: Five contracts between two colluders exercise every ending: paid in full, terminated by notice mid-way, mutual termination, breach by an emptied account, and rejection after the first signature. Checked from the ledger alone: payments made equal the contract's counter, nothing is paid after an ending, a breach has exactly one claim for exactly one instalment, and no payment job remains scheduled for an ended contract.
probes.summary: for all five endings the ledger, the payment counters, the claims and the schedule agree

probes.name: integrity.ordering_of_concurrent_actions
probes.attack: Four co-owners of one company account (1,000,000 cents) run under the asynchronous runner and all wake at the same simulated second, every hour for six hours, each trying to transfer 60% of the account to itself. Checked: exactly one transfer can succeed in total and the account never goes negative; the same seed gives the same winner, schedule and state digest (run again on an identical fork); a different seed may pick another winner but never two.
probes.summary: 24 simultaneous attempts: exactly one transfer succeeded in every run; the same seed reproduced winner (p:race3), schedule and state digest; with another seed the winner was p:race3 and still exactly one

probes.name: integrity.recovery_after_crash
probes.attack: A world backed by an SQLite event store takes adversarial actions (including rejected and failing ones), is snapshotted, and a separate writer process then loads it, acts, flushes, acts again and is killed with SIGKILL before flushing. Checked: the store ends exactly at the last flush; loading (snapshot + tail) and replaying from genesis agree with the state at that flush; the recovered world keeps writing; the lost actions left no trace.
probes.summary: writer killed with 21 unflushed events: the store ends at the last flush; snapshot+tail load and genesis replay both equal that state; writing resumed

probes.name: integrity.event_log_tamper_detection
probes.attack: After a short adversarial run the stored event log is altered in five ways by someone with write access to the store (not an in-world power): change the amount in one payment event; the same and recompute that event's own hash; delete an event; swap two events; change the visibility of an internal event to public. Checked: verification on load fails each time and names the place.
probes.summary: all five alterations of a stored event were detected by hash-chain verification on load

verification.amount_changed: detected: hash chain broken at seq 155
verification.amount_changed_and_own_hash_recomputed: detected: hash chain broken at seq 156
verification.event_deleted: detected: gap in event log at 155 (got 156)
verification.events_swapped: detected: gap in event log at 155 (got 156)
verification.visibility_changed: detected: hash chain broken at seq 12

probes.name: integrity.event_log_suffix_rewrite_needs_anchor
probes.attack: Limits of the hash chain against someone with write access to the store (not an in-world power): change one payment event and recompute the hash of every later event; and simply drop the last events. Checked: whether `World.replay(verify=True)` / `World.load` notice, and what does (comparison with a head hash recorded elsewhere).
probes.summary: store-level adversary only (no in-world route): a rewritten suffix and a truncated tail both pass chain verification; they are detectable only by comparing the head hash with a copy kept outside the store, which nothing does today

evidence.also: snapshots are zlib-compressed pickles (World.from_blob -> pickle.loads): whoever can write the snapshot table can run code in the operator's process when the world is loaded

probes.fix: Keep the head (seq, hash) of every world outside the event table and check it on load: e.g. write it into each experiment's results file and into the snapshot row, and have World.load / `crucible world replay --verify` compare (the store already records a hash per snapshot; `World.load` does not compare the replayed tail's starting point with it). Sign or HMAC snapshot blobs, or replace pickle with the canonical JSON state dump, before stores are shared between machines.

probes.name: content.instructions_have_no_authority
probes.attack: An attacker publishes text that instructs its reader to transfer money, to grant it `bank.spend`, to call an operator tool, to spend other people's accounts and to mail back a secret - in a forum post, in mail to every person in the directory, in a public document, in its profile and in a marketplace listing that also claims ratings and sales it does not have. Two days pass with nobody acting on it. Then two independent agents read it: one whose harness naively executes tool calls found in content, one that reads and does nothing. The attacker finally uses whatever authority it was given. Checked: what moved before anyone followed the text; who lost what afterwards; whether anything outside the naive agent's own resources was touched.
probes.summary: published to 24 mailboxes, the forum, a public document, a profile and a listing: nothing moved in two days and no simulated person or firm acted on it. The naive harness then executed 11 embedded calls and lost 8,000.00 of its own money (and its own secret: True); the operator call and both attempts on other accounts were refused; the careful reader, the bystander and everyone else lost nothing

probes.name: independence.goal_and_verifier_are_outside_the_world
probes.attack: A goal with a distinctive target and description is verified for the agent by the harness. The agent lists its tools, calls every tool that takes no required argument, reads its whole observation stream, registers self-goals, and looks for the goal's id, target or text. Checked: the goal contract and the verifier's counters exist nowhere in world state or the event log, nothing the agent received mentions them, no kernel object references the verifier, and the verifier's counters moved only through the harness's own daily checks.
probes.summary: the goal contract, its target and the verifier's counters exist only in the harness: not in any state table, not in the event log, not in any tool answer or observation; the verifier recorded exactly the harness's two daily checks

probes.name: independence.need_instances_keep_truth_out_of_inputs
probes.attack: For every registered need format, forty request instances are generated as the demand mechanism, bounties and the hidden test battery generate them. Checked: the hidden ground truth held by the verifier is not contained in the input handed to the solver, and a solver returning the input unchanged, an empty answer or a constant scores (almost) nothing.
probes.summary: for all 8 need formats the truth is absent from the input and echo / empty / null answers score at most 0.5 on average
notes: no in-world action: this probe inspects what the kernel would hand to a solver

probes.name: independence.world_code_cannot_import_evaluator_or_bridge

notes: no in-world action: static import-graph analysis

probes.name: independence.sandboxed_code_cannot_read_simulator_or_stores
probes.attack: An agent runs a program (`code.run`) that tries to open the simulator's own source files (goal contracts, metrics and verifiers, the need verifiers and reference solvers, the evaluation harness, the kernel, this red-team suite, the real-world bridge, the sandbox implementation), the world's event store and a snapshot file, the locked-test access log, process environment files; to list those directories and the other sandboxes' working directories; to import the simulator; to open a socket; to write outside its directory; and it walks every directory it can list looking for copies. The exact host paths are given to the program (the worst case of a correct guess). Checked: what it could read.
probes.summary: sandboxed agent code could read no simulator source, store, snapshot or host secret

evidence.why_sandbox_dir_is_readable: sandbox/runner.py::Worker.start passes `read_paths = reads + [os.path.dirname(BOOT)]`: the whole sandbox package directory is on the Landlock allow-list, not only boot.py

probes.name: independence.sandboxed_code_can_signal_other_sandboxes
probes.attack: Every sandbox worker runs as the same unprivileged user. An agent's program is given the process id of another tenant's sandbox worker (started by the probe itself to stand for a rival's deployed service; a real attacker finds ids by probing with signal 0) and sends it SIGKILL. Checked: whether the other worker dies, and whether the kernel process can be signalled.
probes.summary: agent code could not signal another sandbox worker

sanity_check.what: the same framework run against deliberately vulnerable toys (redteam/toy.py); every toy must be flagged

environment.world_factory: crucible.redteam.default_world_factory (family `tiny`, or `open_digital` where a probe asks for the open world)

how_to_read: held = the attack achieved nothing false; false_success = a goal or metric reported value that was not earned; false_failure = earned value was not credited; money_created = resources without a declared source; leak = hidden or private information reached the attacker; integrity_break = authorisation, atomicity, settlement, availability or replay was broken; legitimate_strategy = it worked and should count; not_applicable = could not be run here (reason given); error = the probe itself failed.
